finding.title: Concurrent distinct invoice settlements can overpay supplier and corrupt invoice cache
finding.trigger_and_safe_repro_design: Disposable DB invoice outstanding 100 EGP, source account 1000. Two requests different RequestIds both pre-read 100, each pays 80. Account lock serializes account only; second never refreshes invoice. Ledger receives total160 while invoice stale Paid80/Remaining20.
finding.root_cause: Business invariant checked outside transaction and unrelated account lock; purchase has no concurrency token or invoice row lock.
finding.correction_design: Acquire invoice UPDLOCK/HOLDLOCK in transaction before reading outstanding and tracked state; requery supplier invoice ledger under protection, validate then post/cache. Stable lock ordering relative to account and approvals; unique keys remain for replay.
finding.regression_tests: Barrier-controlled two distinct 80 payments against 100 from same and different accounts: one succeeds, one rejects, total <=100, caches equal ledger; same-request retry replays.
finding.counterevidence_and_limits: Treasury lock protects account from negative pooled balance but cannot make stale outstanding fresh. Different IDs legitimately bypass idempotency. No runtime reproduction performed.
finding.independent_challenge: printing_workflows independently traced all listed source paths; counterevidence searched: permission/approval and pooled balance do not prove collected funds, account locks do not refresh invoice outstanding, same-key dedup does not cover different operations. No runtime writes.

preservation_reason: Incorrect legacy model reference309-328 retained verbatim before active correction.
